voice_text: This second sprint closes gaps that were listed at the end of the first one. It adds sign in lockout, recurring payments with reminders and a monthly summary, family allocation of shared expenses with a contributions report, a personal data download and account deletion, and Hindi and Marathi navigation. It also reports a first performance measurement and an accessibility scan. As before, everything is synthetic demo data.

action: Register a throwaway account; sign out; five wrong passwords; then the correct one.
expected_result: Neutral error five times, then a lockout message.
voice_text: First, protection against password guessing. We create a throwaway account, sign out, and then try the wrong password five times. Each attempt gets the same neutral message, which does not reveal whether the email exists. On the sixth attempt, even the correct password is refused, because the account is locked for fifteen minutes. Resetting the password through the email link unlocks it earlier.
visual_instruction: Register a throwaway account; sign out; five wrong passwords; then the correct one.

action: Sign in as Rahul and open Settings, Notifications.
expected_result: A rent reminder and a September summary.
voice_text: Back as Rahul, the household owner. Rahul has told the system about his monthly house rent on the eighteenth. Because today, in this recording, is the sixteenth of October, the system raised a reminder two days ahead, and also a summary of the previous month with income, expenses and the difference. Both are created only once, however many times the app is opened, and each can be switched off in the preferences.
visual_instruction: Sign in as Rahul and open Settings, Notifications.

action: Open Recurring payments and add a gym membership.
voice_text: The recurring payments tab lists what the household expects every month: rent, internet and an entertainment subscription. Rahul adds a gym membership of fifteen hundred rupees due on the twentieth. The day is validated, so a thirty fifth of the month would be refused. Only people who manage money can change this list; an employee in the business edition cannot.
visual_instruction: Open Recurring payments and add a gym membership.

action: Add a shared expense and split it between members.
voice_text: Now shared household costs. Rahul records a two thousand rupee pantry order and marks it as a shared household expense. A new option lets him allocate the cost between family members. Split equally divides it three ways, down to the paisa. If he changes one share so the total no longer matches, the screen turns red and the server would refuse to save, because allocations must add up to the full amount.
visual_instruction: Add a shared expense and split it between members.

action: Save with a mismatch, then fix and save.
voice_text: Pressing save with the wrong total is refused with a clear message. Rahul corrects it by splitting equally again, and the expense is saved. Each share is stored against the member who bears it.
visual_instruction: Save with a mismatch, then fix and save.

action: Open Reports, Family contributions for October.
voice_text: The new family contributions report compares what each member earned with their share of the shared expenses for the month. The share column adds up to the total of the shared expenses, which is checked by an automated test, and refunds on shared items reduce it. Spending by member also uses these allocations.
visual_instruction: Open Reports, Family contributions for October.

action: Open Settings, Privacy and data, download.
voice_text: Under privacy and data, anyone can download a file with their own profile, memberships and the transactions their role lets them see. The download itself is recorded in the audit history.
visual_instruction: Open Settings, Privacy and data, download.

action: Try to delete the demo account.
voice_text: Deleting an account asks for the password again. This is a shared demo account, so the system refuses, and the demo cannot be broken by accident. Real accounts are deleted, as the next scene shows.
visual_instruction: Try to delete the demo account.

action: Register, delete the account, try to sign in again.
voice_text: We create another throwaway account and delete it. The sign in is closed, the name and email are removed, and because this person is the only member of their workspace, the whole workspace is deleted with it. Trying to sign in afterwards fails. An administrator of a workspace with other members must first hand over the role.
visual_instruction: Register, delete the account, try to sign in again.

action: Sign in as Rahul and switch the language to Hindi, then Marathi, then English.
voice_text: The language menu under the person s name switches the navigation and page titles to Hindi or Marathi. This is a first draft that covers menus and page titles only, and the wording needs review by a native speaker before release. The choice is remembered on this device.
visual_instruction: Sign in as Rahul and switch the language to Hindi, then Marathi, then English.

action: Sign in as Sanjay; open Settings, Recurring payments.
voice_text: The same feature serves the business edition. Sanjay, the finance manager, sees the organization s recurring payments, Azure hosting, office rent and the GitHub subscription, and is reminded three days before each is due. The reminders go to the people who manage money, not to every employee.
visual_instruction: Sign in as Sanjay; open Settings, Recurring payments.

voice_text: Two measurements accompany this sprint, both written up in the sprint report. With twenty five thousand transactions in one organization on PostgreSQL, the dashboard took about one point three seconds, down from eight seconds before the queries were rewritten, and the transaction list about twenty milliseconds. An automated accessibility scan of thirty five page views found no violations after fixes, though it is not a full audit. Still open: a native phone app, a real O C R and language model provider, Redis and S three storage, live ad platform connections, and native speaker review of the translations.
